The exam

ExamAAMI / ACI Certified Radiology Equipment Specialist
CodeCRES
QuestionsUp to 165
Time180 minutes
PassingACI reports CRES results as pass or fail and publishes no cut score. This course's official-format test uses 70%, the same bar as our CBET course.
Lessons60 lessons across 10 units, about 9.9 hours of reading

How the course works

  1. Cheat sheet. Everything the exam expects you to recall cold, printable.
  2. Starter test. A few questions per exam domain, with a confidence rating on each.
  3. Your tutorial. Lessons chosen from what you missed or guessed, each with a checkpoint and a deeper explanation.
  4. Practice tests and retraining. 50 questions, weighted like the real exam. Every miss is explained and feeds back into your lessons.
  5. 3 of your last 5 at 80%. That unlocks one full-length test on the real exam's clock: 165 questions in 180 minutes, at its real passing score of 70%. Pass it once and you are ready to book.

Every lesson

The first 15 lessons are open to read here. Every lesson, with its checkpoint, is free inside the course.

Unit 1: Anatomy, Positioning, and Medical Language

The organs and systems the image shows, the planes and positions radiographers speak in, and the words on a requisition.

  1. Body Organization, Planes, Habitus, and Positional Terminology 9 min
  2. Chest, Abdomen, and Pelvis on the Image: Heart, Lungs, Liver, GI and Urinary Tracts 10 min
  3. Skeleton, Spine, Skull, and Joints, with the Brain, Nervous, and Endocrine Systems 10 min
  4. Positioning by Exam: Projections, Topographical Landmarks, and Reading the Requisition 10 min

On exam day

  • 165 questions in 3 hours, closed book, with an on-screen calculator and notepad. That is over a minute per question; do not rush the math items.
  • Some questions are unscored trial items. A question that seems to be from nowhere may be one of them; answer it and move on.
  • Read for the qualifier: FIRST, MOST likely, BEST. In problem-solving items the first step is usually the patient, then the simplest cause, then the accessory.
  • Know the numbers cold: dose limits, the inverse square law, mAs and the 15 percent rule, heat units, fluoroscopy limits, the leakage limits and their standards.
  • Eligibility is checked when you apply: the technician pathway plus at least 40 percent of your work in radiology over the last two years. Apply early; the windows are May 1 to 15 and November 1 to 15.
  • Two forms of ID, arrive early, sleep the night before.
